chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid said, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Hasan al-Wasiti, on the authority of some of our scholars, on the authority of Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): "Verily, the people in our presence are talking increasingly about the attributes [of Allah]. What do you say?"
He replied: "It is abhorred [makruh]. Do you not hear Allah, the Mighty and High, saying: 'And to your Lord is the end [of all].' Speak about other than that."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on discussing Allah's attributes in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Zurarah queries Imam al-Baqir (AS) regarding the proliferation of speculative discussions on divine attributes (*al-sifah*) among earlier generations. The Imam deems such excessive elaboration *makruh* (disliked), citing the verse 'And to your Lord is the end' to establish that while attributes are affirmed, their essence remains ultimately beyond full human comprehension, urging believers to limit their discourse to what is necessary and avoid boundless speculation.
